name: sign-off
wording: The operator's right, exercised at a gate, to agree that a handover serves its intent, so the work past that gate may go on: signing off a story's read-back starts the story; signing off a plan sends it to be built, the requirements the operator states there binding the lead and its recommendations the lead's to weigh; signing off a pull request lets it merge; signing off release makes the work available to the project's users. Only the operator holds it; anyone else exercises it only where delegated authority grants it, in the operator's place.
reason: The operator and the architect stand in a client engagement with divided authority. The design gave the operator no right of its own between stating intent and release, so a fresh architect asked to read back before recording read back and recorded in the same turn. Sign-off is the operator's right, kept apart from the gate where it is exercised.
